Bring the proof kits for my open PRs up to date with today's proof-kit harness. You are the orchestrator: decide which kits need work, run one subagent per kit that does, put their QA questions to me, and do every Roam step yourself, one kit at a time.

Read first: the proof-kit skill (~/.claude-company/skills/proof-kit/SKILL.md) and /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/README.md.

What changed in the harness on 2026-10-05 (kits made earlier may break these):
1. Every approved case needs real steps, or is a check made only of expect.js. proof/__tests__/kits.test.ts fails if any shipped kit has a case with only an intent.
2. Obsidian cases live in their own eng-XXXX-obsidian.json kit (model it on kits/eng-2195.json). A Roam kit's page can't drive Obsidian.
3. The published proof runner (roam-prototypes PR #26, at the previews URL) shows a checklist and points the PR's own CI build at the proof database in the browser. A local build in target.dist is only needed for terminal takes.
4. The proof database runs on 127.0.0.1:55321. Builds pointed at 54321 are refused.
5. Kits that don't touch a database use dg-baseline@2. Database kits keep dg-baseline@1 or their own fixtures, and they run only on my machine; don't propose a hosted test database.
6. After a push, confirm Roam finished saving (push gives up after 120 s). Connect this machine with: sh ~/.local/share/dg-proof/open.sh 'dg-proof://connect'

Which PRs (as of 2026-10-05; re-check with: gh pr list -R DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph --author sid597 --state open):
- Open, with a kit: #1485 ENG-2194 (kits/eng-2194.json, Roam), #1484 ENG-2267 (kits/eng-2267.json, Obsidian), #1479 ENG-2296 (kits/eng-2296.json, Roam).
- Open, no kit: #1493 ENG-2329 and #1412 ENG-2143. Ask me whether either gets a kit.
- Skip: #1508 ENG-2176 (updated today), #1486 and #1468 (not ticket work), and kits whose PRs are merged (eng-2195, eng-2348, eng-2349, eng-2350, eng-2351).

Step 1, triage (you; reads only, no Roam). For each kit: run prove.ts --kit <kit> --coverage, check take-readiness (takeReadiness in proof/take.ts), check for Obsidian cases inside a Roam kit, check baseline and needs against item 5, and check target.pr against the open PR. Show me a table (kit / needs work? / why). A kit that passes everything gets no subagent.

Step 2, subagents (one per kit that needs work; model sonnet; run them in parallel). Each runs the proof-kit write stage for its kit, plus qa if the kit has no QA areas yet, from that PR's worktree apps/roam (/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-XXXX; never cd to the main checkout). Give each these rules:
- Edit only your own kit files. No git commit, stash or push. Don't touch other kits, the runner or roam-prototypes.
- Don't open Roam: no push, probe, inspect, load-url, --check, live, take or post.
- Keep case ids and existing decisions.
- Script every case's steps from the code. If a path can't be read from the code, return the question instead of leaving an intent.
- For qa: run qa.ts propose, then stop and return the proposed cases (title, area, intent). You can't ask sid yourself.
- Before returning, run --coverage and check your own kit's take-readiness. Return what changed, coverage, readiness and any open questions.

Step 3, my decisions. Ask me each subagent's QA questions with AskUserQuestion (one question per case, up to four per call, options as the skill says). Record them with qa.ts decide, then resume each subagent with SendMessage to script the approved cases and move Obsidian ones to the Obsidian kit.

Step 4, checks. From any apps/roam: pnpm exec tsx --test /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/__tests__/*.test.ts. Everything must pass.

Step 5, Roam (you only, one kit at a time). Every Roam command opens the same slot-3 browser profile, which only one process can hold, so never run two at once, and wait if another session is in a Roam stage. For each Roam kit: ask me before using --replace on an existing page, push, confirm Roam finished saving, and count the page's case:: blocks against the kit. Connect this machine once at the end. Obsidian kits have no page; give me each one's take command instead (/proof-kit eng-XXXX-obsidian take).

Finish with a table: kit / what changed / tests / page link.

---
name: proof-kit
description: Take a ticket's proof kit through its stages, from writing the cases off the ticket's Done When to QA, a Roam run, a live rehearsal, the recorded take and posting it on the PR. Use when sid types /proof-kit, or asks to write, check, QA, build, run, rehearse, record or post a ticket's proof kit. For a PR video without a kit, use pr-video.
argument-hint: "<ticket> [status|write|red|qa|build|check|roam|live|take|post] [flags]"
---

# Proof kits for a ticket

Invocation: `/proof-kit $ARGUMENTS`

A proof kit is a ticket's proof written as cases before the code: the ticket
cases prove its Done When, QA cases cover what the change could break next
to it. Everything about kits is in `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/README.md`;
read the section a stage names before running it the first time in a session.

Paths used below:

- `P=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof`
- `K=$P/kits/eng-XXXX.json`, the kit; its `name` is `eng-XXXX`
- `OUT=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/output/proof`, one folder per run (`<kit>-<time>/`, with `report.md`)
- Run every command from `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam`, or
  from the worktree's `apps/roam` in a worktree session (its `node_modules` must exist).

The stages and the flags each takes are in `stages.json` beside this file.
The prompt band (the `proof-kit-band` mod) shows the same list while sid
types `/proof-kit`, so a new stage or flag goes into `stages.json` in the
same session it's added to the tools.

## Read the invocation

The words can come in any order:

- The kit: a ticket (`ENG-2348`, `eng-2348` or `2348` all mean the kit `eng-2348`),
  or a kit's own file name in `$P/kits` (`eng-2176-obsidian`, `roam-selftest`).
- The stage: one of the names in `stages.json`.
- Flags: words starting with `--`, with a value after the ones `stages.json` gives `values`.
  A flag that isn't listed for the stage is a mistake: say so and ask, never guess what it meant.

## Ask for what's missing

Sid won't remember the options, so show them when he leaves them out:

1. **No ticket.** Take it from the session's branch or worktree name (`eng-XXXX`)
   when there is one. Otherwise ask with AskUserQuestion: the newest kits in
   `$P/kits` (by modified time, up to 3), and "Other" for a new ticket.
2. **No stage.** Run `status` (it only reads), then ask with AskUserQuestion:
   the stage `status` names as next first, marked "(Recommended)", then up to
   three others that fit the kit's state. Each option's description says what
   the stage does and whether it opens Roam.
3. **A stage with `presets` and no flags given.** Ask once with the presets
   as options, the default first. A stage without presets runs with its
   defaults, and the reply lists the flags it could have taken in one line.

Never ask about something the invocation already says.

## Stages

**status** (reads only). No kit file: next is `write`. Otherwise run
`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --coverage` (cases by decision, QA areas,
Done When coverage; opens nothing), note `target.pr` and whether
`target.dist` holds an `extension.js`, and read the newest `report.md` under
`$OUT/eng-XXXX-*`. Next is the first of these that applies: coverage fails
→ `write`; no PR yet → implement (`red` first if sid wants to see the kit
fail); no QA areas, or cases still `proposed` → `qa`; the kit needs the
database and the dist is missing or older than the PR's head → `build`;
approved cases with only an `intent` → `write` (script their steps; the
kits test fails while any remain), or `live` when the path can't be read
from the code; otherwise `take`, then `post`.

**write** (code only). Read the ticket with the Linear MCP (`get_issue`).
Read the README's "The kit", "cases", "prepare", "needs" and "Done When"
sections, and model the kit on `kits/eng-2348.json` (needs the database) or
`kits/roam-selftest.json` (UI only); recipes are in `$P/recipes/`.
- At least one case per Done When bullet, its `proves` naming the bullet
  (`"Done When 2: <the bullet's words>"`).
- Every approved case gets `steps`, or is a check made only of `expect.js`,
  before the stage ends: recipes, command palette labels exactly as registered,
  selectors from the code, and fixtures for the data it needs (node types,
  pages, relation types, settings). Don't leave a case with only an `intent`:
  `$P/__tests__/kits.test.ts` requires every shipped kit to be ready for an
  unattended take, so one intent-only case fails it for every session. When a
  path truly can't be read from the code, ask sid instead.
- Cases in Obsidian go in their own kit, `kits/eng-XXXX-obsidian.json`
  (`target.app: "obsidian"`; model it on `kits/eng-2195.json`), with steps
  from the `proof.obsidian` helpers and Obsidian's command palette. A Roam
  kit's page and its live rehearsal can't drive Obsidian. Each kit covers
  the Done When bullets it can prove in its own app.
- `expect.js` when code can tell (the `proof.*` helpers), `expect.text`
  when a person judges.
- `title`, `claim` and `given` in plain words, because the panel and the HUD explain the run with them.
- `baseline: "dg-baseline@2"` (sync and node sharing off), and
  `target: { "slot": "3", "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-XXXX" }` plus
  `"pr": <n>` once the PR exists.
- `needs: ["supabase", "embed-stub"]`, with its own fixtures turning sync or
  node sharing on, only when the feature reads or writes the database
  (`dg-baseline@1` still turns both on, for older kits). A kit without it
  runs from a shared Roam link on the PR's CI build, for anyone.
- When updating a kit, keep case ids and decisions as they are.

Finish with `--coverage` passing for each kit, and
`pnpm exec tsx --test $P/__tests__/kits.test.ts` passing.

**red** (opens Roam, optional). This proves the kit fails before the fix. It only works
before the PR exists (no `target.pr`) and for a kit that doesn't connect to
a database (main's CI build talks to production, and the runner refuses
it). `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts push --kit $K --build main --title proof/eng-XXXX-main`
prints the page's link. Give it to sid to open and Run. A case that passes
on main proves nothing about the fix: rewrite it.

**qa** (code only, plus a Sonnet call). This needs `target.pr` and a worktree on the
PR's branch. Run `npx tsx $P/qa.ts propose --kit $K [--base <ref>] [--model <m>]`,
then `npx tsx $P/qa.ts list --kit $K`. Ask about the proposed cases with
AskUserQuestion, one question per case and up to four per call. Each
question carries the case's title, area and intent, with the options
"Approve", "Reject: this PR doesn't reach it" and "Reject: another case
covers it" ("Other" takes sid's own reason). Record the answers with
`qa.ts decide --kit $K --approve <ids>`, then one
`qa.ts decide --kit $K --reject <id> --reason "<why>"` per rejection, since a reason belongs to its case.
Approved QA cases arrive with only an intent: script their steps the way
`write` says, and move the Obsidian ones (with their decision, and their area
from `surface`) into the Obsidian kit. Finish with the kits test passing.

**build** (code only). Run `npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --build`. It needs `target.pr`,
`target.dist` and a worktree at the PR's pushed head. It bakes in the proof
database and the embeddings stub when the kit needs them.

**check** (opens Roam). For a database kit, start the database and the stub first (below). Then
`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --check [--slot n]`.

**roam** (opens Roam). `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts push --kit $K [--replace]` prints the link;
nothing else is needed beforehand, even for a database kit. The page's
checklist does the rest: **Connect this machine** starts the proof database,
the stub and the keys server through the `dg-proof://` handler (set up on
sid's machine; another developer runs `pnpm helper setup --dg <checkout>`
once in roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner), the PR's
CI build is pointed at the proof database in the browser, **Set up and load**
applies the graph setup, and **Ask your agent** opens an agent on by-hand
cases. Push refuses a page that already has a kit. `--replace` deletes that
kit's block, its runs log and any edits made on the page (the panel edits
the page), and nothing pulls page edits back into the JSON yet. Ask before
replacing.

Push waits 120 s for Roam to save and can give up on a long page (a
186-block page took 144 s). The unsaved writes stay in the slot's profile, so
open the page again with `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts probe --js "<expr>"`, wait
until `.rm-sync__icon` has `rm-sync--synced`, and count the page's `case::`
blocks against the kit. For a database kit, connect this machine yourself so
the checklist starts at ✓: `sh ~/.local/share/dg-proof/open.sh 'dg-proof://connect'`
runs what the Connect button runs, and `curl -s 127.0.0.1:8766/status` should
report the database. Then give sid the link. Only one session drives the
slot's Roam window at a time, so don't push while another session is in a
Roam stage.

**live** (opens Roam). For a database kit, start the database, the stub and the build first.
Run `npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --live [flags]` in the background with a
log. Tell sid to watch workspace 9 and steer from the HUD; pressing Stop twice
ends it. After it ends, compare `diff -u $K <run folder>/kit.proposed.json`,
summarize what the rehearsal added, and ask whether to keep it (copy it over the kit).

**take** (opens Roam, records). A take refuses cases that are only an intent, js
nobody allowed and cases still waiting for a decision. Rehearse those with
`live` first. In the ticket's implementation session, hand the take to a
subagent (Sonnet) with the exact command; elsewhere, run it here. For a
database kit, start the database, the stub and the build first. Run
`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K [flags]` in the background with a log and a
timeout. The run folder holds `report.md` and the video. Check the video as
pr-video's "Verify before sharing" says.

**post** (outward). Show sid the report and ask before posting anything.
Post the report with
`gh api repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/issues/<pr>/comments -F body=@<report.md>`
(`gh pr edit` fails on this repo). For the video, follow pr-video's "Getting
the mp4 onto the PR".

Starting the database and the stub, when the kit needs them:
`npx tsx $P/db.ts up`, and `python3 /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/recorder/embed-stub.py`
in the background (port 3210).

## Rules

- A stage marked `opensRoam` runs only when sid named it, or picked it in
  this invocation's question. Never start one on your own, and never run
  one as a follow-on from another stage. These stages run headed on workspace
  9, on slot 3 unless `--slot` says otherwise, and never against discourse-dev-graph.
- Tests never touch the production database. The tools refuse a kit that would
  connect on a CI build. Don't get around that with `--allow-*` flags or another build.
- No screenshots. The commands report text.
- Runs that take minutes (`live`, `take`, `qa propose`) go in the background
  with a log, and you report progress from the log.
- End every stage with what it produced (paths, the link, counts) and one
  line naming the next stage.
----
# Proof kits

Proof-driven development: write the proof before the feature. A proof kit
holds everything one PR's proof needs, written out ahead:

- what must be running (the proof database, the embeddings stub, the PR's build),
- the data to prepare, each piece with a check so prepared data is skipped,
- the cases and what counts as working, including cases Claude proposed from
  the PR's diff for the areas next to the change, each approved or rejected
  with the reason kept,
- the captions for the video.

`prove.ts` runs a kit. It checks the needs, prepares only what's missing,
then records the narrated video (the default) or rehearses it live in front
of you. The report and the video are the PR's proof. When the data is
already in place, a run starts in seconds, so a kit is as easy to rerun and
share as a video.

## Run a kit

From `discourse-graph/apps/roam` (for its tsx and playwright):

```bash
PROVE="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/prove.ts"
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --coverage   # the kit against its Done When; opens nothing
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --check   # what's missing, changes nothing
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json           # record the video
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --live    # rehearse it with you
```

- `--coverage` validates the kit and prints its cases by decision and its
  Done When coverage, without a browser, a build or the database, so a
  session writing code can check a kit it just wrote. `--check` opens a
  Roam session to look at the before-load data.
- `/proof-kit <ticket> [stage] [flags]` (the `proof-kit` Claude skill) walks
  a ticket through these commands; its stages and flags are in
  `~/.claude-company/skills/proof-kit/stages.json`, which the
  `proof-kit-band` mod shows above the prompt while you type the command.
- `--kits a.json,b.json` runs several kits one after another with the same
  flags and prints where each report and video landed. A failed kit doesn't
  stop the rest.
- Kits run on slot 3 (test-3-graph). discourse-dev-graph is refused unless
  you pass `--allow-dev-graph`.
- A kit that touches a database needs the proof database up (see below):
  `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts up`. Runs read its
  keys from `proof/db/.env`; `SUPABASE_*` exported in your shell are ignored.
- Every run writes `output/proof/<kit>-<timestamp>/`: `journal.jsonl` (every
  event), `report.md` (ready to post as a PR comment), plus the video, or the
  proposed kit and the footage for a rehearsal.
- Other flags (`--dist`, `--slot`, `--url`, `--allow-login`,
  `--allow-stale-build`, `--no-narrate`, `--mode`, `--speed`, `--dwell`) are
  listed at the top of `prove.ts`.

What a run does, in order:

1. **Needs.** Each need is checked, and a failure prints the command that
   fixes it. The dist must have the right env baked in, and when the kit names
   a PR, the dist's `buildCommit` must be the PR's head.
2. **Outside fixtures.** Database rows and anything else done from the shell:
   check, apply only if missing, check again.
3. **Before-load fixtures.** Flags and node types, which the extension reads
   once at load. They run in a session without the extension, Roam gets time
   to sync the writes, and a fresh session confirms them.
4. **The session.** In-session fixtures (pages, settings Roam resets on every
   load) and the baseline's smoke checks run first. In a take they're trimmed
   off the video. Then the cases run.
5. **The report.**

## The proof database

Kits never touch the hosted (production) database, and no longer share the
stack you develop against either. They get their own local Supabase:

- **Native, no Docker.** It runs on the Supabase CLI's experimental stack
  (`[experimental] stack = true`), pinned to 2.119.0 in `proof/db/package.json`
  and installed there on first use. Its data lives in `~/.supabase/stacks/`.
- **Its own ports.** The API is `127.0.0.1:55321`, Postgres `55322` (the
  checkout's 543xx moved to 553xx), so it runs beside main's Docker stack on
  54321 and any worktree's. Analytics, mail and edge functions stay off.
  `core/database.ts` holds the address; every path in proof uses it.
- **A checkout's schema.** `db.ts up` writes `proof/db/supabase/` from
  `discourse-graph/packages/database/supabase` (config, migrations, schemas)
  and brings the database to those migrations: new ones apply in place, and
  when one it applied changed or is gone (switching from a PR's worktree back
  to main) it resets. `--from <worktree>` tests a PR's own migrations.
- **Seeded with what kits name.** The dev graph (space 66566) and the
  Obsidian test vault (106039) as publish sources, test-3-graph (120237), each
  with its anonymous account, the authors 3 and 106041, and the
  `eng-2329-demo` group all three are in. Generated ids start at 200000.

```bash
DB="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts"
$DB up [--from <checkout>]   # start, migrate, seed, write proof/db/.env
$DB status                   # answering? which checkout's schema?
$DB reset                    # back to the migrations, seeded again
$DB sql "select id, url from \"Space\""
$DB stop                     # data stays for the next up
```

Builds for kits (`prove.ts --build`) bake in the proof database and the
embeddings stub, or no database at all when it isn't set up and the kit
doesn't need one. They never inherit a dev stack's env or fall back to
discoursegraphs.com's API.

## Done When: the cases against the ticket

Each case says which of the ticket's Done When bullets it covers, in
`proves`: by number (`"Done When 2: Enabling Stored Relations removes the
warning."`) or by quoting the bullet. Every run reads the ticket from Linear
(`LINEAR_API_KEY`) and prints each bullet with the cases that cover it.
`--check` fails when a bullet has no case, a number is past the last bullet,
or a numbered case's words read like a different bullet (the ticket's bullets
moved, or the kit counted wrong). A take report opens with the bullets, each
checked when every case under it passed, then the other cases.

- The ticket is the kit's `ticket` (`"ENG-2348"`), else the `eng-####` in the
  kit's name, else in its PR's branch. Without a key or a ticket the run says
  so and goes on.
- A `proves` that names no bullet ("case 1's result, shown on screen") is
  fine: the case is listed as not tied to a Done When. QA cases usually are.
- Only approved cases count; a rejected case covers nothing.

## QA: what else the change could break

A kit's own cases prove the ticket. `qa.ts` covers what the change could break
next to it: Claude reads the PR's diff, lists the areas it reaches, and
proposes cases a person can test by hand. Someone approves or rejects each one.
A rejected case stays in the kit with its reason, so the record shows what was
left out and why. Approved cases run like any other case: by hand in a live
rehearsal or the in-Roam runner, and unattended in a take once a rehearsal has
written their steps.

```bash
QA="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/qa.ts"
$QA propose --kit kits/eng-2348.json     # areas + proposed cases, from the PR's diff
$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json      # asks about each proposed case: approve, reject (with why), skip
$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json --approve <ids> --reject <ids> --reason "<why>"
$QA list --kit kits/eng-2348.json        # areas, and every case by decision
```

- `propose` needs the PR's worktree (found from `target.pr`, or `--worktree`)
  and the `claude` CLI. It diffs the worktree against where it left
  `origin/main` (`--base` to change), and Claude (Sonnet unless `--model`)
  may only read files there. The diff, the prompt and the answer are kept in
  `output/proof/<kit>-qa-<time>/`. Run it again after a push: areas and cases
  the kit already has, rejected ones included, aren't proposed again.
- `decide` records who decided (`git config user.name`, or `--by`) and when.
  Each answer is saved as it's given.
- A take refuses while any case is still proposed. A live rehearsal and the
  in-Roam runner play the approved cases and say how many wait or were
  rejected.
- Reports list the rejected cases with their reasons, the cases still
  waiting, and each area with the approved cases that cover it.

## The kit

```json
{
  "name": "eng-2348",
  "title": "Warn when sharing or importing with Stored Relations off",
  "baseline": "dg-baseline@1",
  "target": { "slot": "3", "pr": 1506, "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-2348" },
  "needs": ["supabase", "embed-stub"],
  "prepare": [
    {
      "id": "stored-relations-off",
      "why": "Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for",
      "phase": "in-session",
      "check": { "js": "..." },
      "apply": { "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Open - Discourse settings" }, "why": "open settings" }] }
    }
  ],
  "cases": [
    {
      "id": "share-warning",
      "title": "Share warns when Stored Relations is off",
      "caption": "Sharing with Stored Relations off now warns before anything leaves the graph.",
      "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Discover shared nodes" }, "why": "open import the way a user would" }],
      "expect": { "js": "if (!document.body.innerText.includes('Stored Relations')) throw new Error('No warning.')" }
    }
  ]
}
```

### needs

`"supabase"` (the proof database answers on 127.0.0.1:55321), `"embed-stub"` (the
stub answers on 127.0.0.1:3210) and `"env:NAME"` are built in. A custom need
is `{ "id", "why", "check": "<shell, exit 0 when met>", "fix": "<what to run>" }`.
Needs the kit implies are added on its own: a `rest` or `sql` fixture needs
Supabase and the service key, and every `{{env.NAME}}` needs `NAME`.

### prepare

Each fixture is `{ id, why, phase, check?, apply, settleMs? }`.

| phase | when it runs | check | apply |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outside` | before any browser | `{ "command" }` (exit 0 = present) or `{ "rest": { "path", "expect": "rows" \| "none" } }` | `{ "command" }`, `{ "sql" }` (psql into the proof database) or `{ "rest": { "method", "path", "body?" } }` |
| `before-load` | in a session without the extension | `{ "js" }`, truthy = present | `{ "js" }` |
| `in-session` | once the extension loads, before the cases | `{ "js" }` | `{ "js" }`, or `{ "steps" }` for things only the UI can set |

- js checks and applies are expressions, like a `js` step. Use an async IIFE
  for several statements.
- A fixture without a check runs every time. Use that for settings Roam resets
  on each load.
- `rest` reaches the proof database's REST API with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- `{ "publish": { space, author, group, types, nodes } }` (outside) writes
  what another space's publish would have: node types (`{ id, label, format,
  template? }`), nodes (`{ id, type, title, body? }`) with their Document and
  direct and full Content rows, and ResourceAccess for the group. The
  space's platform picks the shapes Roam or Obsidian write. It's all upserts,
  so leave out the check and it runs on every take. test-3-graph is in the
  `eng-2329-demo` group with the dev graph (space 66566, author 3) and the
  Obsidian test vault (space 106039, author 106041), so either can be the
  source.
- The proof database runs without edge functions, so a Roam kit that touches
  the database signs in before load: the `database-session` fixture in the
  shipped kits runs `proof.supabase.signIn({ serviceKey, publishableKey })`.
  It makes what create-space would have (the graph's Space row, its
  anonymous account with the password the graph stores, PlatformAccount and
  editor access) and writes the session the extension reads. Its check,
  `proof.supabase.signedIn()`, asks the proof database whether it knows the
  session's user, so a session from another stack (DG keys every local one
  `sb-127:`) or from before a reset signs in again.
- Name what a kit creates with `{{ns}}` (the kit's namespace) so cleanup can
  find it and kits don't collide in a shared test graph.

### cases

- `steps`: recordDemo actions, each with a one-line `why`. `source` says who
  wrote a step: `kit`, `model` or `you`. js from `model` or `you` runs only
  after you allow it on the HUD, which sets `approved: true`.
- `intent`: plain language. A case with only an intent needs a live rehearsal,
  where the brain works out its steps.
- `expect.js` runs in the page; throwing fails the case. `expect.text` needs
  your eyes: you give the verdict live, and in a take the video is the
  evidence. A case can be only an `expect.js` check.
- `proves` names the Done When bullet the case covers (see "Done When"
  above); `checks` says in plain words what its `expect.js` checks.
- `decision` is `{ status: proposed | approved | rejected, by, at, reason }`.
  A case without one was written by hand and counts as approved; only
  approved cases run, and a rejected case needs its `reason`. `surface` names
  the area (from the kit's `surface` list) a case checks. `qa.ts` writes both.
- `caption` and `toast` are for the take: the narration line and the
  top-right flash. Write captions the way the pr-video skill says.
- `{ "when": { "js", "do": [actions] } }` runs its actions only when the js
  is truthy, so a toggle (the Discourse context overlay, say) can be turned
  on without turning it off on the next run. Its js counts as js for the
  Allow rule.

### templates

Any string can use `{{env.NAME}}`, `{{kit}}`, `{{run}}` and `{{ns}}`. They're
filled only when the string runs, so keys never land in a kit, a proposed
kit or a generated storyboard on disk.

## Obsidian kits

A kit with `target.app: "obsidian"` (plus `vault`, `cdp`, `pr` and `dist`)
attaches over CDP to an Obsidian you started on the test vault with
`--remote-debugging-port=9223`, and records through `recordObsidian.ts`.
Takes and `--check` only; live rehearsals drive Roam. No baseline and no
before-load fixtures, since the app is already running. `--build` builds
apps/obsidian in the PR's worktree with the local database and the stub,
stages it in `dist` with `build-commit.txt`, and installs `main.js` and
`styles.css` in the vault, keeping the replaced files as `*.pre-<kit>`. A
take rebuilds and reinstalls when the vault runs another kit's build, and
reloads the plugin before anything else. `proof.obsidian` has the vault
helpers: `nodeType`, `importedFiles`, `removeNodeTypes`, `open`, `write`,
`setTemplates`, `notices`, `closeModals`. The palette action types into
Obsidian's palette.

## Take: the video

The default. It needs nobody at the screen, so it refuses a kit with
intent-only cases, js you haven't allowed, or cases still waiting for a
decision, and says which. It writes a
small storyboard module that builds the storyboard from the kit when
recordDemo loads it, then runs `recorder/recordDemo.ts --narrate --cursor`
unchanged. Fixtures and smoke checks go in the storyboard's `setup`, which
recordDemo runs before scene 1 and trims off the video. The report marks each
case pass, fail, shown (checked by eye, see the video) or not run, with the
time it starts in the video (`video 1:05`), and says when setup or the video
assembly failed instead. The recorder logs each scene's start in the finished
video and embeds them as chapters in the mp4, so a player can jump from case
to case.

## Live: a rehearsal you steer

`--live` runs the kit in front of you on workspace 9. Steps the kit knows
replay through recordDemo's `runAction` with no model involved. A case written
only as an intent, a failed step, or something you ask for in chat goes to the
brain: a Claude Code session, ideally on Haiku, told to read this file. What
works is baked into `kit.proposed.json`. Review it with `diff -u`, and move it
over the kit to keep it. The rehearsal's report gives each case's time in the
session footage (`footage 4:10`), so a by-hand test has its place in the
recording. The session stays open after the last case so you can
add cases, and ends when you press Stop twice on the HUD or the brain sends
`stop`.

### The HUD

A panel in the bottom-right corner (⇆ moves it left), in a closed shadow root
that page scripts and Playwright selectors can't reach. While a step runs it
stays on screen but lets every click through.

- At the top, what the kit proves (`claim`) and the setup it starts from
  (`given`). Then every case with ✓, ✗ or ▶, what it proves (`proves`), and
  for the current case its steps with the running one highlighted and what it
  checks at the end (`checks`). Write those four fields in plain words; they
  are what the panel has to explain the run with.
- A feed of what just happened: steps, checks with their failure reason,
  what you said and what the agent answered.
- Pause or Resume, Next (one step, or skip the hold), − and + for speed
  (0.25× to 4×), and the mode (auto, step, case).
- ✓ Pass and ✗ Fail: the verdict a case waits for, or end the current case
  early when you spot a bug.
- Allow or Deny: the only way js the agent wrote can run.
- The ask box: what you type goes to the agent as a `said` event, and its
  answer comes back into the feed. The dot is green while an agent is
  listening; with none, what you type is saved as a note.
- Ctrl+Alt+Space pauses or resumes; Ctrl+Alt+. runs the next step.

193	# Proof kits
194	
195	Proof-driven development: write the proof before the feature. A proof kit
196	holds everything one PR's proof needs, written out ahead:
197	
198	- what must be running (the proof database, the embeddings stub, the PR's build),
199	- the data to prepare, each piece with a check so prepared data is skipped,
200	- the cases and what counts as working, including cases Claude proposed from
201	  the PR's diff for the areas next to the change, each approved or rejected
202	  with the reason kept,
203	- the captions for the video.
204	
205	`prove.ts` runs a kit. It checks the needs, prepares only what's missing,
206	then records the narrated video (the default) or rehearses it live in front
207	of you. The report and the video are the PR's proof. When the data is
208	already in place, a run starts in seconds, so a kit is as easy to rerun and
209	share as a video.
210	
211	## Run a kit
212	
213	From `discourse-graph/apps/roam` (for its tsx and playwright):
214	
215	```bash
216	PROVE="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/prove.ts"
217	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --coverage   # the kit against its Done When; opens nothing
218	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --check   # what's missing, changes nothing
219	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json           # record the video
220	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --live    # rehearse it with you
221	```
222	
223	- `--coverage` validates the kit and prints its cases by decision and its
224	  Done When coverage, without a browser, a build or the database, so a
225	  session writing code can check a kit it just wrote. `--check` opens a
226	  Roam session to look at the before-load data.
227	- `/proof-kit <ticket> [stage] [flags]` (the `proof-kit` Claude skill) walks
228	  a ticket through these commands; its stages and flags are in
229	  `~/.claude-company/skills/proof-kit/stages.json`, which the
230	  `proof-kit-band` mod shows above the prompt while you type the command.
231	- `--kits a.json,b.json` runs several kits one after another with the same
232	  flags and prints where each report and video landed. A failed kit doesn't
233	  stop the rest.
234	- Kits run on slot 3 (test-3-graph). discourse-dev-graph is refused unless
235	  you pass `--allow-dev-graph`.
236	- A kit that touches a database needs the proof database up (see below):
237	  `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts up`. Runs read its
238	  keys from `proof/db/.env`; `SUPABASE_*` exported in your shell are ignored.
239	- Every run writes `output/proof/<kit>-<timestamp>/`: `journal.jsonl` (every
240	  event), `report.md` (ready to post as a PR comment), plus the video, or the
241	  proposed kit and the footage for a rehearsal.
242	- Other flags (`--dist`, `--slot`, `--url`, `--allow-login`,
243	  `--allow-stale-build`, `--no-narrate`, `--mode`, `--speed`, `--dwell`) are
244	  listed at the top of `prove.ts`.
245	
246	What a run does, in order:
247	
248	1. **Needs.** Each need is checked, and a failure prints the command that
249	   fixes it. The dist must have the right env baked in, and when the kit names
250	   a PR, the dist's `buildCommit` must be the PR's head.
251	2. **Outside fixtures.** Database rows and anything else done from the shell:
252	   check, apply only if missing, check again.
253	3. **Before-load fixtures.** Flags and node types, which the extension reads
254	   once at load. They run in a session without the extension, Roam gets time
255	   to sync the writes, and a fresh session confirms them.
256	4. **The session.** In-session fixtures (pages, settings Roam resets on every
257	   load) and the baseline's smoke checks run first. In a take they're trimmed
258	   off the video. Then the cases run.
259	5. **The report.**
260	
261	## The proof database
262	
263	Kits never touch the hosted (production) database, and no longer share the
264	stack you develop against either. They get their own local Supabase:
265	
266	- **Native, no Docker.** It runs on the Supabase CLI's experimental stack
267	  (`[experimental] stack = true`), pinned to 2.119.0 in `proof/db/package.json`
268	  and installed there on first use. Its data lives in `~/.supabase/stacks/`.
269	- **Its own ports.** The API is `127.0.0.1:55321`, Postgres `55322` (the
270	  checkout's 543xx moved to 553xx), so it runs beside main's Docker stack on
271	  54321 and any worktree's. Analytics, mail and edge functions stay off.
272	  `core/database.ts` holds the address; every path in proof uses it.
273	- **A checkout's schema.** `db.ts up` writes `proof/db/supabase/` from
274	  `discourse-graph/packages/database/supabase` (config, migrations, schemas)
275	  and brings the database to those migrations: new ones apply in place, and
276	  when one it applied changed or is gone (switching from a PR's worktree back
277	  to main) it resets. `--from <worktree>` tests a PR's own migrations.
278	- **Seeded with what kits name.** The dev graph (space 66566) and the
279	  Obsidian test vault (106039) as publish sources, test-3-graph (120237), each
280	  with its anonymous account, the authors 3 and 106041, and the
281	  `eng-2329-demo` group all three are in. Generated ids start at 200000.
282	
283	```bash
284	DB="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts"
285	$DB up [--from <checkout>]   # start, migrate, seed, write proof/db/.env
286	$DB status                   # answering? which checkout's schema?
287	$DB reset                    # back to the migrations, seeded again
288	$DB sql "select id, url from \"Space\""
289	$DB stop                     # data stays for the next up
290	```
291	
292	Builds for kits (`prove.ts --build`) bake in the proof database and the
293	embeddings stub, or no database at all when it isn't set up and the kit
294	doesn't need one. They never inherit a dev stack's env or fall back to
295	discoursegraphs.com's API.
296	
297	## Done When: the cases against the ticket
298	
299	Each case says which of the ticket's Done When bullets it covers, in
300	`proves`: by number (`"Done When 2: Enabling Stored Relations removes the
301	warning."`) or by quoting the bullet. Every run reads the ticket from Linear
302	(`LINEAR_API_KEY`) and prints each bullet with the cases that cover it.
303	`--check` fails when a bullet has no case, a number is past the last bullet,
304	or a numbered case's words read like a different bullet (the ticket's bullets
305	moved, or the kit counted wrong). A take report opens with the bullets, each
306	checked when every case under it passed, then the other cases.
307	
308	- The ticket is the kit's `ticket` (`"ENG-2348"`), else the `eng-####` in the
309	  kit's name, else in its PR's branch. Without a key or a ticket the run says
310	  so and goes on.
311	- A `proves` that names no bullet ("case 1's result, shown on screen") is
312	  fine: the case is listed as not tied to a Done When. QA cases usually are.
313	- Only approved cases count; a rejected case covers nothing.
314	
315	## QA: what else the change could break
316	
317	A kit's own cases prove the ticket. `qa.ts` covers what the change could break
318	next to it: Claude reads the PR's diff, lists the areas it reaches, and
319	proposes cases a person can test by hand. Someone approves or rejects each one.
320	A rejected case stays in the kit with its reason, so the record shows what was
321	left out and why. Approved cases run like any other case: by hand in a live
322	rehearsal or the in-Roam runner, and unattended in a take once a rehearsal has
323	written their steps.
324	
325	```bash
326	QA="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/qa.ts"
327	$QA propose --kit kits/eng-2348.json     # areas + proposed cases, from the PR's diff
328	$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json      # asks about each proposed case: approve, reject (with why), skip
329	$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json --approve <ids> --reject <ids> --reason "<why>"
330	$QA list --kit kits/eng-2348.json        # areas, and every case by decision
331	```
332	
333	- `propose` needs the PR's worktree (found from `target.pr`, or `--worktree`)
334	  and the `claude` CLI. It diffs the worktree against where it left
335	  `origin/main` (`--base` to change), and Claude (Sonnet unless `--model`)
336	  may only read files there. The diff, the prompt and the answer are kept in
337	  `output/proof/<kit>-qa-<time>/`. Run it again after a push: areas and cases
338	  the kit already has, rejected ones included, aren't proposed again.
339	- `decide` records who decided (`git config user.name`, or `--by`) and when.
340	  Each answer is saved as it's given.
341	- A take refuses while any case is still proposed. A live rehearsal and the
342	  in-Roam runner play the approved cases and say how many wait or were
343	  rejected.
344	- Reports list the rejected cases with their reasons, the cases still
345	  waiting, and each area with the approved cases that cover it.

347	## The kit
348	
349	```json
350	{
351	  "name": "eng-2348",
352	  "title": "Warn when sharing or importing with Stored Relations off",
353	  "baseline": "dg-baseline@1",
354	  "target": { "slot": "3", "pr": 1506, "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-2348" },
355	  "needs": ["supabase", "embed-stub"],
356	  "prepare": [
357	    {
358	      "id": "stored-relations-off",
359	      "why": "Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for",
360	      "phase": "in-session",
361	      "check": { "js": "..." },
362	      "apply": { "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Open - Discourse settings" }, "why": "open settings" }] }
363	    }
364	  ],
365	  "cases": [
366	    {
367	      "id": "share-warning",
368	      "title": "Share warns when Stored Relations is off",
369	      "caption": "Sharing with Stored Relations off now warns before anything leaves the graph.",
370	      "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Discover shared nodes" }, "why": "open import the way a user would" }],
371	      "expect": { "js": "if (!document.body.innerText.includes('Stored Relations')) throw new Error('No warning.')" }
372	    }
373	  ]
374	}
375	```
376	
377	### needs
378	
379	`"supabase"` (the proof database answers on 127.0.0.1:55321), `"embed-stub"` (the
380	stub answers on 127.0.0.1:3210) and `"env:NAME"` are built in. A custom need
381	is `{ "id", "why", "check": "<shell, exit 0 when met>", "fix": "<what to run>" }`.
382	Needs the kit implies are added on its own: a `rest` or `sql` fixture needs
383	Supabase and the service key, and every `{{env.NAME}}` needs `NAME`.
384	
385	### prepare
386	
387	Each fixture is `{ id, why, phase, check?, apply, settleMs? }`.
388	
389	| phase | when it runs | check | apply |
390	|---|---|---|---|
391	| `outside` | before any browser | `{ "command" }` (exit 0 = present) or `{ "rest": { "path", "expect": "rows" \| "none" } }` | `{ "command" }`, `{ "sql" }` (psql into the proof database) or `{ "rest": { "method", "path", "body?" } }` |
392	| `before-load` | in a session without the extension | `{ "js" }`, truthy = present | `{ "js" }` |
393	| `in-session` | once the extension loads, before the cases | `{ "js" }` | `{ "js" }`, or `{ "steps" }` for things only the UI can set |
394	
395	- js checks and applies are expressions, like a `js` step. Use an async IIFE
396	  for several statements.
397	- A fixture without a check runs every time. Use that for settings Roam resets
398	  on each load.
399	- `rest` reaches the proof database's REST API with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
400	- `{ "publish": { space, author, group, types, nodes } }` (outside) writes
401	  what another space's publish would have: node types (`{ id, label, format,
402	  template? }`), nodes (`{ id, type, title, body? }`) with their Document and
403	  direct and full Content rows, and ResourceAccess for the group. The
404	  space's platform picks the shapes Roam or Obsidian write. It's all upserts,
405	  so leave out the check and it runs on every take. test-3-graph is in the
406	  `eng-2329-demo` group with the dev graph (space 66566, author 3) and the
407	  Obsidian test vault (space 106039, author 106041), so either can be the
408	  source.
409	- The proof database runs without edge functions, so a Roam kit that touches
410	  the database signs in before load: the `database-session` fixture in the
411	  shipped kits runs `proof.supabase.signIn({ serviceKey, publishableKey })`.
412	  It makes what create-space would have (the graph's Space row, its
413	  anonymous account with the password the graph stores, PlatformAccount and
414	  editor access) and writes the session the extension reads. Its check,
415	  `proof.supabase.signedIn()`, asks the proof database whether it knows the
416	  session's user, so a session from another stack (DG keys every local one
417	  `sb-127:`) or from before a reset signs in again.
418	- Name what a kit creates with `{{ns}}` (the kit's namespace) so cleanup can
419	  find it and kits don't collide in a shared test graph.
420	
421	### cases
422	
423	- `steps`: recordDemo actions, each with a one-line `why`. `source` says who
424	  wrote a step: `kit`, `model` or `you`. js from `model` or `you` runs only
425	  after you allow it on the HUD, which sets `approved: true`.
426	- `intent`: plain language. A case with only an intent needs a live rehearsal,
427	  where the brain works out its steps.
428	- `expect.js` runs in the page; throwing fails the case. `expect.text` needs
429	  your eyes: you give the verdict live, and in a take the video is the
430	  evidence. A case can be only an `expect.js` check.
431	- `proves` names the Done When bullet the case covers (see "Done When"
432	  above); `checks` says in plain words what its `expect.js` checks.
433	- `decision` is `{ status: proposed | approved | rejected, by, at, reason }`.
434	  A case without one was written by hand and counts as approved; only
435	  approved cases run, and a rejected case needs its `reason`. `surface` names
436	  the area (from the kit's `surface` list) a case checks. `qa.ts` writes both.
437	- `caption` and `toast` are for the take: the narration line and the
438	  top-right flash. Write captions the way the pr-video skill says.
439	- `{ "when": { "js", "do": [actions] } }` runs its actions only when the js
440	  is truthy, so a toggle (the Discourse context overlay, say) can be turned
441	  on without turning it off on the next run. Its js counts as js for the
442	  Allow rule.
443	
444	### templates
445	
446	Any string can use `{{env.NAME}}`, `{{kit}}`, `{{run}}` and `{{ns}}`. They're
447	filled only when the string runs, so keys never land in a kit, a proposed
448	kit or a generated storyboard on disk.
449	
450	## Obsidian kits
451	
452	A kit with `target.app: "obsidian"` (plus `vault`, `cdp`, `pr` and `dist`)
453	attaches over CDP to an Obsidian you started on the test vault with
454	`--remote-debugging-port=9223`, and records through `recordObsidian.ts`.
455	Takes and `--check` only; live rehearsals drive Roam. No baseline and no
456	before-load fixtures, since the app is already running. `--build` builds
457	apps/obsidian in the PR's worktree with the local database and the stub,
458	stages it in `dist` with `build-commit.txt`, and installs `main.js` and
459	`styles.css` in the vault, keeping the replaced files as `*.pre-<kit>`. A
460	take rebuilds and reinstalls when the vault runs another kit's build, and
461	reloads the plugin before anything else. `proof.obsidian` has the vault
462	helpers: `nodeType`, `importedFiles`, `removeNodeTypes`, `open`, `write`,
463	`setTemplates`, `notices`, `closeModals`. The palette action types into
464	Obsidian's palette.
465	
466	## Take: the video
467	
468	The default. It needs nobody at the screen, so it refuses a kit with
469	intent-only cases, js you haven't allowed, or cases still waiting for a
470	decision, and says which. It writes a
471	small storyboard module that builds the storyboard from the kit when
472	recordDemo loads it, then runs `recorder/recordDemo.ts --narrate --cursor`
473	unchanged. Fixtures and smoke checks go in the storyboard's `setup`, which
474	recordDemo runs before scene 1 and trims off the video. The report marks each
475	case pass, fail, shown (checked by eye, see the video) or not run, with the
476	time it starts in the video (`video 1:05`), and says when setup or the video
477	assembly failed instead. The recorder logs each scene's start in the finished
478	video and embeds them as chapters in the mp4, so a player can jump from case
479	to case.
480	
481	## Live: a rehearsal you steer
482	
483	`--live` runs the kit in front of you on workspace 9. Steps the kit knows
484	replay through recordDemo's `runAction` with no model involved. A case written
485	only as an intent, a failed step, or something you ask for in chat goes to the
486	brain: a Claude Code session, ideally on Haiku, told to read this file. What
487	works is baked into `kit.proposed.json`. Review it with `diff -u`, and move it
488	over the kit to keep it. The rehearsal's report gives each case's time in the
489	session footage (`footage 4:10`), so a by-hand test has its place in the
490	recording. The session stays open after the last case so you can
491	add cases, and ends when you press Stop twice on the HUD or the brain sends
492	`stop`.
493	
494	### The HUD
495	
496	A panel in the bottom-right corner (⇆ moves it left), in a closed shadow root
497	that page scripts and Playwright selectors can't reach. While a step runs it
498	stays on screen but lets every click through.
499	
500	- At the top, what the kit proves (`claim`) and the setup it starts from
501	  (`given`). Then every case with ✓, ✗ or ▶, what it proves (`proves`), and
502	  for the current case its steps with the running one highlighted and what it
503	  checks at the end (`checks`). Write those four fields in plain words; they
504	  are what the panel has to explain the run with.
505	- A feed of what just happened: steps, checks with their failure reason,
506	  what you said and what the agent answered.
507	- Pause or Resume, Next (one step, or skip the hold), − and + for speed
508	  (0.25× to 4×), and the mode (auto, step, case).
509	- ✓ Pass and ✗ Fail: the verdict a case waits for, or end the current case
510	  early when you spot a bug.
511	- Allow or Deny: the only way js the agent wrote can run.
512	- The ask box: what you type goes to the agent as a `said` event, and its
513	  answer comes back into the feed. The dot is green while an agent is
514	  listening; with none, what you type is saved as a note.
515	- Ctrl+Alt+Space pauses or resumes; Ctrl+Alt+. runs the next step.
516	
517	### The brain's loop
518	
519	```bash
520	CTL="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/ctl.ts"
521	$CTL status
522	$CTL events '{"since":0,"waitMs":20000}'
523	$CTL steps - < steps.json
524	```
525	
526	Run it from `discourse-graph/apps/roam`. Wait for `PROOF READY` in the
527	runner's output, then long-poll `events` with the last `seq` you saw:
528	
529	| Event | What to do |
530	|---|---|
531	| `need-steps` | Read `intent`, `expect` and `aria` (the page as an aria snapshot). Send steps: `{"caseId":"...","steps":[...]}`. |
532	| `step-failed` | Read `error` and `aria`. Send a fix with `"how":"replace-failed"`, or `retry`, `skip-step`, or ask sid. |
533	| `need-approval` | Tell sid what the js does and that it waits on the HUD. You can't approve it. |
534	| `need-verdict` | Optionally check with `aria`, `text` or `query`, then propose `{"verdict":"pass","reason":"..."}`. Sid decides. |
535	| `case-end`, `cases-done` | Summarize briefly. After `cases-done`, ask whether to add cases or stop. |
536	| `session-end` | Report the paths the runner printed. |
537	| `said` | sid typed this in the panel. Do what it asks with the commands below, then answer in one or two plain sentences with `reply {"text":"..."}`. Questions ("why did it click that?") get a `reply` only. |
538	
539	When sid talks, in the panel's ask box (a `said` event) or in your chat:
540	
541	- "pause", "faster", "next", "step mode": `pause`, `speed {"speed":2}`,
542	  `next`, `mode {"mode":"step"}`.
543	- "do X instead": `pause`, write the steps, send them with
544	  `"how":"insert-next"` or `"replace-rest"` and `"by":"you"`, then `resume`.
545	- "why are you doing that?": `status` has the current step's `why` and `source`.
546	- "also test X": `add-case` with `{"by":"you","case":{"title":"...","intent":"..."}}`.
547	- A remark worth keeping: `note` with `{"text":"...","by":"you"}`.
548	
549	Writing steps: prefer clicks, typing and the command palette over js (they're
550	visible and need no Allow). Selectors are Playwright selectors; take names from
551	the aria snapshot instead of guessing. Read-only commands run freely: `aria`,
552	`text`, `query` (Datalog for `roamAlphaAPI.q`), `screenshot`, `console`. The
553	engine README's Roam pitfalls apply: click a Blueprint checkbox's
554	`.bp3-control-indicator`, match command palette labels exactly.
555	
556	Never point a kit at discourse-dev-graph, kill the runner, or type
557	credentials. If the profile is logged out, stop and hand it to sid.

559	## In Roam: kits on pages
560	
561	A kit can also live on a Roam page and run from there, with no terminal: you
562	share the page's link, whoever opens it gets the PR's build and the kit in
563	the right sidebar, and Run plays every case in their own browser. The runner
564	is the proof-runner prototype in DiscourseGraphs/roam-prototypes, a Roam
565	developer extension anyone loads once per graph:
566	
567	> Settings > Roam Depot > Developer extensions (developer mode on) > Load from URL >
568	> `https://discoursegraphs.com/releases/prototypes/previews/proof-runner/proof-runner/`
569	
570	(That's PR #26's preview; the stable `…/prototypes/proof-runner/` exists once
571	it merges, and `roam/links.ts` names the one in use.) The first block on
572	every kit page says this, for a visitor without the runner; once the runner
573	is on, that block hides. The prototype's README has the roam/js loader for
574	graphs that use that instead.
575	
576	What opening a kit page does:
577	
578	1. The runner reads the page's `{{proof}}` block: `build:: <branch>` names a
579	   CI build on Vercel Blob (the files `discoursegraphs.com/releases/roam/<branch>/`
580	   serves), `pr:: <n>` looks the branch up on GitHub.
581	2. The panel opens with a checklist of what the kit needs before Run, one
582	   line per need that applies: the runner, this machine (for a kit that
583	   needs the database), the graph setup, the build, the database session,
584	   and the agent (for by-hand cases). A met line is ✓; one that isn't shows
585	   the one button that meets it. When every line is met they fold into one,
586	   and Run is one press.
587	3. It checks the kit's before-load fixtures (baseline included). When any
588	   would change the graph, the checklist lists what will change and waits
589	   for **Set up and load**; otherwise the build loads straight away. A
590	   fixture needing a `{{env.X}}` key the browser doesn't have is skipped
591	   with a note.
592	4. A kit that needs a database (or turns on sync or node sharing) runs on
593	   the PR's CI build pointed at the proof database: before the build runs,
594	   the runner swaps its Supabase URL and key for the proof database's and
595	   DG's website API for the embeddings stub, and refuses a build where
596	   anything of the hosted stack is left. The keys come from this machine's
597	   helper; until it answers, the checklist offers **Connect this machine**
598	   (see below).
599	5. It loads the build and checks the commit inside `extension.js` against the
600	   PR's head (the CDN can lag an upload by a minute). Loaded as an extension,
601	   the runner hands the build its own `extensionAPI` (settings under `dg:`);
602	   from roam/js the build gets a stand-in that keeps settings in the browser.
603	6. The kit block opens pinned at the top of the right sidebar with the run
604	   panel: the HUD's layout, its controls, verdict buttons and feed. During a
605	   run the panel shows the page's own case blocks (Roam's `renderBlock`), not
606	   a copy: the case running now is open with its steps, the others show
607	   their `case::` line with a verdict and note beside it. Editing a step in
608	   the panel edits the page. Every rendering of a case block, in the panel
609	   and on the page, gets a colored edge for its verdict; the step running
610	   now is tinted and the steps done are dimmed.
611	7. Run plays in-session fixtures and baseline smoke checks, then the cases.
612	   A case with only an `intent` is done by hand: the panel says what to do
613	   and waits for Done, then the check or your verdict; or **Ask your agent**
614	   writes its steps (see below). A finished run adds a
615	   line to the block's `runs` list: verdicts, build and commit, time, who.
616	8. A run keeps the kit it started with. The one exception: when a step
617	   fails, fix its block in the panel and press Retry, and the fixed step
618	   runs (as the kit's own, without an Allow). Every other edit applies from
619	   the next Run.
620	
621	One build per tab: a tab that has loaded none loads a kit page's build when
622	you navigate to it, and a tab with a different build offers "Reload with
623	this build". A run that stops can resume from the next case after a reload.
624	If DG is already running (installed from Roam Depot), the runner doesn't load
625	a second copy and says so.
626	
627	### Where the code lives
628	
629	- `proof/core/`: the browser-clean shared core (kit validation, machine,
630	  recipes, fixtures-to-steps, template, journal, helpers, action types). The
631	  Node files (`kit.ts`, `machine.ts`, …) re-export it and add file and shell
632	  work.
633	- `proof/roam/`: the in-page runner (page format, selectors, input,
634	  executor, panel, build loader, entry), plus `build.ts` and `cli.ts`, which
635	  run in Node.
636	- `roam/build.ts` writes `roam/data.ts` (recipes and baselines as JSON
637	  imports), copies `core/`, `roam/`, the recipes, baselines and kits (as test
638	  fixtures, local paths stripped) into
639	  `roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner/`, and runs that repo's build. The
640	  prototype's `src/index.ts` (the `runExtension` wrapper), README and tests
641	  belong to the prototype.
642	
643	### The page
644	
645	A kit page reads like a manual test script. Steps are sentences; the action
646	sits folded under each one.
647	
648	```
649	{{proof}} Warn when sharing with Stored Relations off
650	  kit:: eng-2348
651	  pr:: 1506
652	  baseline:: dg-baseline@1
653	  prepare
654	    Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for
655	      ```json {"id": "stored-relations-off", "phase": "in-session", ...}```
656	  case:: Discover shared nodes warns while Stored Relations is off
657	    id:: import-warns
658	    open import the way a user would
659	      use:: discover.open
660	    expect js:: `proof.waitFor(() => proof.callout('Stored relations are disabled'))`
661	  case:: Search keeps working
662	    intent:: run Node Search for "PK baseline" and look at the results
663	    expect:: the baseline nodes show and no sync error appears
664	  case:: Overlay counts stay right
665	    intent:: open a node with relations and hover the overlay
666	    area:: `s-discourse-context-overlay`
667	    decision:: rejected
668	    decided by:: sid
669	    reason:: the overlay isn't touched by this PR's code path
670	  surface
671	    Discourse context overlay
672	      id:: `s-discourse-context-overlay`
673	      why:: it reads the relation cache the diff changes
674	      files:: `src/cache.ts`
675	```
676	
677	An action is `use:: <recipe>` (plus `with:: {json}`), `<kind>:: <value>` for
678	any action kind (`palette::` for command_palette), or a code block:
679	` ```javascript ` for js, ` ```json ` for any action. Put values in inline
680	code so Roam leaves brackets alone. Plain blocks under the root are notes. An
681	attribute the parser doesn't know is an error, so a typo can't leave a case
682	without its check.
683	
684	### From a terminal
685	
686	`proof/roam/cli.ts` drives the same signed-in slot profiles (slot 3 by
687	default), headed. From `discourse-graph/apps/roam`:
688	
689	```bash
690	R=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/roam/cli.ts
691	npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/roam/build.ts   # sync into roam-prototypes and build
692	npx tsx $R serve                            # serve that build on 127.0.0.1:8765, for load-url
693	npx tsx $R load-url --url <release dir>     # add the runner via Roam Depot's Load from URL
694	npx tsx $R push --kit kits/eng-2348.json    # write proof/eng-2348; prints its link (--build, --pr, --replace)
695	npx tsx $R run --title proof/eng-2348 --verdict pass --done   # open the link fresh, press Run, report
696	npx tsx $R inspect --title proof/eng-2348   # what the loader decided and what the panel says
697	```
698	
699	`run --set-up` presses Set up and load for kits that ask. Releases are cached
700	for a day and Roam loads URL extensions through the browser cache, so after
701	publishing a new runner pass `--clear-cache` (or hard-reload by hand). `install` and
702	`uninstall` put or remove the prototype's roam/js loader on `proof/runner`.
703	`push` and the other commands wait for Roam's sync icon to settle before
704	closing, since a closed tab drops writes that haven't reached the server.
705	`kits/roam-selftest.json` checks the runner itself: build load, palette,
706	Escape on a dialog, a recipe, a fixture and a by-hand case, with sync and
707	sharing off. The Playwright harness's developer-extension loader removes
708	every developer extension in the slot, the runner's too; add it back with
709	`load-url` after a take.
710	
711	### How it differs from Playwright
712	
713	- Input is made in the page: clicks wait for the target to be visible,
714	  enabled, still and not covered (the error names what covers it), keys carry
715	  `keyCode`/`which` so Blueprint dialogs close on Escape, and typing goes
716	  through `insertText`. Selectors understand the Playwright forms kits use:
717	  `:has-text()`, `:text()`, `:visible`, `>> nth=N`, `text=`.
718	- `command_palette` runs the registered command by label; the palette UI is
719	  the fallback.
720	- `screenshot` steps are skipped, and `open` only follows hash routes.
721	- CI builds are compiled against the production database, and tests never
722	  run there. A kit that needs a database, or has (or turns on) sync or node
723	  sharing, runs on the PR's CI build pointed at the proof database in the
724	  browser (step 4 above), on the machine that has the proof database. No
725	  local build is needed. Kits that only exercise UI run on CI builds as
726	  they are, for anyone: `dg-baseline@2` turns sync and node sharing off,
727	  where `dg-baseline@1` turned them on (and so needed the database).
728	
729	### This machine: Connect
730	
731	The checklist's **Connect this machine** opens a `dg-proof://connect`
732	link, which the proof helper on the machine answers: it brings up the
733	embeddings stub and the proof database when they're down, then answers on
734	`127.0.0.1:8766` with the proof database's address and the kits' env (the
735	runner fills `{{env.SUPABASE_*}}` from it, in that tab only). The panel waits
736	for it, then carries on loading. The machine line's **Disconnect** stops
737	the helper and what it started. Chrome asks once before roamresearch.com may
738	open the link and reach localhost; allow both.
739	
740	The helper is `proof/helper/` (database, stub, server, link handler, CLI),
741	and `roam/build.ts` ships it with the runner in roam-prototypes, so any
742	developer sets a machine up once, from their roam-prototypes checkout:
743	
744	```bash
745	cd roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner     # Node 22 or later
746	pnpm helper setup --dg <their discourse-graph checkout>   # --runtime docker|native, --workdir <dir>
747	```
748	
749	Setup remembers the checkout (whose migrations make the schema), runs
750	Supabase in Docker when Docker answers (natively otherwise), keeps the
751	database's files in `~/.local/share/dg-proof/db` (macOS: `~/Library/Application
752	Support/dg-proof/db`, Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dg-proof\db`), and registers
753	`dg-proof://` links: xdg on Linux, a small AppleScript app on macOS, registry
754	keys under the user on Windows (Docker only there). `pnpm helper start | stop |
755	status | uninstall` do the rest by hand. The prototype's README, "Getting set
756	up", is the developer's guide. This machine runs the source here instead, through tsx and
757	the proof database at `proof/db`:
758	
759	```bash
760	npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/helper/cli.ts setup --dg /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph --runtime native --workdir /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db
761	```
762	
763	The handler's log is `~/.local/share/dg-proof/handler.log`.
764	
765	### Your agent: Roam's MCP
766	
767	When Roam has its AI API (`extensionAPI.ai.addTool`), the runner registers
768	tools an agent connected to the graph (Roam's MCP, through a Local API
769	token) can call: `proof_status` (the cases, the checklist, where a run
770	stands), `proof_snapshot` (the page, its dialogs and their controls, for
771	selectors), `proof_control` (run, pause, resume, next, retry, skip, stop),
772	`proof_add_steps` (steps for the case waiting on them, written under the
773	case's block and run) and `proof_fix_step` (the failed step's block
774	rewritten and run). Js an agent writes waits for an Allow in the panel, and
775	verdicts are the person's. The checklist's **Ask your agent** opens a
776	`dg-proof://agent` link: the handler opens a kitty window with `claude` told
777	which kit to drive (the prompt also goes on the clipboard, for an agent
778	that's already open). The tools work where Roam's Local API reaches the
779	page, which is the Roam desktop app.
780	
781	## Safety
782	
783	- The control socket is a Unix socket in a 0700 directory with a fixed command
784	  list: no TCP port and no Node-side eval.
785	- Only the HUD can approve js or give a final verdict, and it only accepts calls
786	  with the per-session nonce from the page's main frame.
787	- Steps from the socket can't `open` another origin, and `screenshot` names
788	  can't contain slashes. Fixtures come only from the kit file, never the socket.
789	- The proof helper binds to 127.0.0.1, answers only roamresearch.com
790	  (others get 403): `GET /status` hands out the proof database's address
791	  and the kits' env (Supabase's stock keys for a stack that holds only test
792	  data) and `POST /stop` stops it. Disconnect when you're done.
793	- `dg-proof://` links carry nothing the handler runs: `connect` takes no
794	  arguments, and `agent` takes a graph name and a block uid it checks, and
795	  hands the agent its prompt through the environment, never a shell.
796	- A PR build pointed at the proof database is checked after the swap: if any
797	  hosted Supabase URL, hosted key or DG website API is left, it doesn't run.
798	- In Roam, a kit page's js runs without an Allow: whoever can edit the graph
799	  can run code for whoever presses Run, the same trust roam/js already asks
800	  for. Keep kit graphs to the team. The loader only fetches builds from DG's
801	  blob store, where only PRs from the repo itself upload, and runs the exact
802	  text whose commit the panel shows. Keys set with `setSecret` stay in that
803	  browser's storage and never go into the graph.
804	
805	## Tests
806	
807	From `discourse-graph/apps/roam`:
808	
809	```bash
810	pnpm exec tsx --test /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/__tests__/*.test.ts
811	```
812	
813	They use fakes and a headless test page. `db-live.test.ts` also signs a
814	stand-in graph in to the proof database from a page served as
815	roamresearch.com, and skips when the database isn't up. None of them open Roam;
816	`roam/cli.ts run` with `kits/roam-selftest.json` is the live check for the
817	in-Roam runner.

A re-upsert would write the node's current title and edit time over its older stored body, so importers would skip its next publish. Each error has a different cause, and I've confirmed both.

**1. "`area::` isn't a case field": your browser is running an old copy of the proof runner.**
The runner published at the previews URL accepts `area::`, `decision::`, `decided by::`, `decided at::` and `reason::`; I downloaded it and checked its field list. The list in your error stops at `expect js`, so your tab loaded a copy from before those fields were added. Roam loads URL extensions through the browser cache, and these releases are cached for a day. All four pages will hit this, because every one has QA cases with `area::`.

To fix it, open Roam Depot > Developer Extensions and click the ⟳ refresh next to the proof-runner URL (top right in your second screenshot). A hard reload with Ctrl+Shift+R also works.

**2. "No build at …/eng-2143-…/extension.js (404)": CI has never built the Roam extension for #1412.**
- **Why there's no build:** the "PR - Roam To Blob Storage" workflow only runs when a PR's own diff touches `apps/roam/**` or the shared packages. #1412 sits on top of `eng-2143-source-adapters-base`, and its own diff is 6 files, none under `apps/roam`. So that workflow has never run for it.
- **The other pages are fine:** the CI builds for ENG-2194, ENG-2296 and ENG-2329 all return 200.
- **A build of the branch wouldn't help anyway:** it's 79 commits behind main. The Roam behaviour this kit tests (`[[@placeholder]]` and automatic source import) only exists on main.

I should have checked that each build existed before pushing the pages, and I didn't.

**Fix options for ENG-2143:**
- **Merge main into #1412 and push (recommended).** Michael's open review already needs this. Compared with its old base, the merge touches `apps/roam`, so CI uploads a build of main plus the PR's tests, and the page then loads it. First the PR's tests have to switch from `(source missing)` to `[[@placeholder]]`, or CI fails. I can do that in the eng-2143 worktree and run the checks, then show you before anything is pushed.
- **Or skip the page for ENG-2143.** Its Roam half would then run only as a terminal take on a local build.

Which do you want? Meanwhile I'm noting the build gotcha in memory so future kits check for the build first.

# Proof kits: handoff (2026-10-02)

Proof-driven development: write the proof kit first, then the feature. A kit
(`proof/kits/<name>.json`) holds needs, data preparation (each fixture with a
check), cases, and captions. `prove.ts` runs it: by default a take (the
narrated video through recordDemo), `--live` a rehearsal you steer, `--check`
a dry look, `--build` only builds and stages the PR's dist.

## Where things are

- Code: `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/` (local repo, no remote).
  Commits: `f4cd177` (core) and the handoff commit after it.
- Docs: `proof/README.md` (kit format, modes, the brain's loop).
- Design page: https://claude.ai/artifact/DJpiWk9CdUDSyCwvUNnpsV (version 4).
  Part two covers proof kits, the live rehearsal, sharing, decisions and
  build order.
- recordDemo changes: exports `CURSOR_INIT_SCRIPT`, and storyboards gained
  `init` (scripts loaded in every document) and `setup` (actions before scene
  1, trimmed off the video).

## In-Roam runner (2026-10-03)

Kits run from a Roam page: share the link, whoever opens it gets the PR's
build and the kit pinned in the right sidebar, Run plays it. README section
"In Roam: kits on pages" has the page format, the code layout and the CLI.

**Rule: tests never touch the production database.** CI compiles PR builds
against production Supabase (`zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz`), the same one users
have. On 2026-10-03 the four v1 kits were run in Roam on CI builds with sync
on, which put test-3-graph on production (a Space row, sid's account row,
its discourse nodes and embeddings; nothing was published). That was wrong.
Sync and node sharing are off in test-3-graph again. The production rows
still need deleting by someone with production access.

### Kit pages just work: checklist, Connect, pointed builds, agent tools (built 2026-10-05)

terminal commands, the setup note at the top and only when needed, and a
way to connect his local agent through Roam's MCP.

content.text:
Today your outs depend on what went wrong.

| What happens | Your out today |
|---|---|
| A step fails | The panel shows the error with **Retry**, **Skip step** and **Skip case**. If the step itself is wrong, edit its block right there in the panel and press Retry. |
| The run seems stuck | It's waiting on you for one of four things: **Next** (step mode), a **✓ Pass / ✗ Fail** verdict, **Done** on a by-hand case, or **Allow / Deny**. Once the new runner reaches your tab, the status line says which. |
| You think the PR is broken | Press **✗ Fail**. That records the verdict with your note and moves to the next case. |
| You want out entirely | Press **Stop** twice. Verdicts so far are kept, and after a reload you get **Resume from case N**. |
| The graph or database is now in a weird state | No out from the page. You'd have to ask me in the terminal to re-run its setup, or run `db.ts reset`. |

**"Ask your agent"** opens a Claude window told which kit to drive. It can write steps for by-hand cases and fix a failed step. But it reaches the page only through Roam's Local API, which only the **Roam desktop app** has. In a browser tab it can't see or drive the page.

So the real gap is the last row. My recommendation is one out you never have to think about:

- **A "Stuck?" button**, always on the panel and the floating bar. It pauses the run and offers, in plain words:
  1. Try this step again (edit it first if it's wrong)
  2. Skip this step or this case
  3. "The PR is broken here": Fail with a note, then move on
  4. Hand it to Claude, with the case, the step, the error and the page state already in the prompt
  5. Start over clean
- **Start over clean** is the real reset: reload the tab, apply all of the kit's setup again (Roam-side and database), then Run. For the database part, the helper on this machine would run the kit's `publish`, `sql` and `rest` fixtures against the proof database, never shell commands. That makes every page run start from the same state, the way a terminal take does.
- **A kit-writing rule:** anything a case changes gets put back by setup at the start of every run, so a run that dies halfway can't leave things dirty. I'd fix ENG-2194's trigger and ENG-2267's node types to follow it.

That's a decent chunk of runner work, and it changes what the helper is allowed to do: a kit page could make it run SQL against the local proof database. Should I build it?

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.
